name: Constellation Energy
description: Constellation is the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in the US: it owns the nation's biggest nuclear fleet (about 22 GW at 14 stations, 183 TWh in 2025) and, since it bought Calpine on January 7, 2026, a large natural gas and geothermal fleet, for about 55 GW in total. It is not a regulated utility: it sells the power to businesses, utilities, cities and homes at negotiated prices, mostly through long-term contracts, so profit depends on power prices and contract terms rather than a regulator-set return. Data-center demand is the growth story: it has a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 (now Crane Clean Energy Center) and a 20-year agreement with Meta for Clinton starting June 2027. 2025 revenue was 25.5 billion dollars and GAAP net income 2,319 million (adjusted operating earnings 2,944 million, or 9.39 dollars per share). Calpine cost 21.8 billion dollars in stock and cash; regulators required selling several plants, including about 4.4 GW to LS Power.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge (Independent Power Producers is the closer sub-industry for some peers; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source). SEC SIC code 4911 (Electric Services). Constellation owns no regulated utility: it sells power at market prices, which is why the utility label misleads.

businessLines.name: Mid-Atlantic
businessLines.shareBasis: 6,487 of 21,968 million total reportable segment electric revenues (consolidated operating revenues 25,533 million include 4,370 million Other and -805 million unrealized hedge losses)
businessLines.how: Sells nuclear and other output plus retail supply to businesses and homes under contracts and at wholesale market prices, plus capacity payments; revenue net of purchased power and fuel drives profit.
businessLines.description: Generation and sales in the eastern half of PJM (NJ, MD, VA, WV, DE, DC and parts of PA and NC); 10,386 MW, 33% of 2025 capacity.

businessLines.name: Midwest
businessLines.how: Same model as Mid-Atlantic; includes nuclear plants such as Clinton, whose output goes to Meta from June 2027 under a 20-year agreement.
businessLines.description: Western half of PJM and MISO (excluding its Southern Region); 11,606 MW, 37% of 2025 capacity, the largest region.

businessLines.name: New York
businessLines.how: Wholesale and retail power sales plus state Zero Emission Credit payments (New York Clean Energy Standard runs to 2049 for its upstate nuclear plants).
businessLines.description: NYISO market; FitzPatrick, Ginna and Nine Mile Point nuclear plants; 3,093 MW, 10% of capacity.

businessLines.name: ERCOT
businessLines.how: Sells power at Texas market prices plus retail; profit is more exposed to Texas price spikes than the rest of the fleet.
businessLines.description: Texas grid; 4,742 MW, 15% of 2025 capacity before Calpine. Calpine adds a much larger Texas gas fleet from 2026.

businessLines.name: Other Power Regions
businessLines.how: Mostly selling power to commercial and industrial customers and homes in competitive retail markets; 5,583 million dollars of revenue from only 5% of capacity means it mainly resells purchased power.
businessLines.description: New England, South, West and Canada; 1,849 MW, 5% of capacity, but a large customer-facing (retail and commercial) business.

businessLines.name: Calpine (acquired January 7, 2026)
businessLines.how: Sells power from combined-cycle gas and geothermal plants at market prices and through contracts, plus retail supply; adds a gas-heavy fleet to a nuclear-heavy company.
businessLines.description: About 23 GW across 72 generation and battery assets after divestitures (21 GW natural gas plus the Geysers geothermal assets, the largest geothermal portfolio in the US) and a retail platform selling about 62 TWh a year. Not in the FY2025 segment figures; included from Q1 2026.

brands.name: Nuclear fleet
brands.share: About 22 GW of 31.7 GW owned capacity pre-Calpine (sum of segments); 183 TWh of 204.9 TWh total owned supply in 2025, about 89% (computed; nuclear TWh may be at ownership share); capacity factor 94.7%

brands.name: Natural gas and oil
brands.share: About 7 GW pre-Calpine, 6% of 2025 electric supply; Calpine adds 21 GW of gas

brands.name: Renewables (hydro, wind, solar)
brands.share: About 2.6 GW, 2% of 2025 electric supply; Calpine adds the Geysers geothermal assets

brands.name: Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart)
brands.share: About 835 MW once operating; 20-year Microsoft PPA; up to 1.0 billion dollars DOE loan guarantee issued November 2025

whatsNext.text: Sale of five PJM plants (about 4.4 GW, mostly gas, Delaware and Pennsylvania) to LS Power for 5.0 billion dollars before adjustments, required by regulators; a further 606 MW Brazos Valley plant in ERCOT to LS Power for 860 million dollars agreed August 2026 (last required sale). Closings subject to approvals
Clinton nuclear output goes to Meta under a 20-year PPA starting June 2027, supporting relicensing for another two decades
